Wenjun Li  
Email: wli@vitaltechinnovations.com | Location: Bengaluru, India | Phone: +91 9876543210  

Professional Experience  
For the past 11 years, I have focused on developing embedded systems for healthtech applications, with a emphasis on reliability and scalability. At VitalTech Innovations, I transitioned from firmware development to leading embedded engineering initiatives, contributing to the design of medical IoT devices that meet FDA standards. My work includes architecting edge computing solutions for real-time patient monitoring, which reduced latency by 35% through optimized data routing. I also mentored junior engineers in RTOS design, enabling them to integrate hardware peripherals with minimal power overhead. Earlier, as a firmware developer at VitalTech, I led the implementation of secure MQTT communication with 99.98% reliability, ensuring compliance with HIPAA regulations. At MediSense Medical Devices, my intern role involved creating low-power sensor nodes for wearable health monitors, achieving a 22% reduction in battery consumption through C/C++ code optimization. These experiences have shaped my ability to balance hardware constraints with software performance in mission-critical environments.  

Education  
Master of Science in Electrical Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (2015). Thesis work focused on power-efficient signal processing for biomedical sensors, which informed my approach to embedded system design. Prior to graduate studies, I completed a Bachelor’s in Electrical Engineering from Tsinghua University (2012).  

Technical Skills  
C/C++ forms the foundation of my work, from writing real-time control logic for medical devices to mentoring teams on memory management techniques. I have integrated Embedded Linux into several projects, including a wearable ECG monitor that required kernel-level customization for low-latency data capture. IoT protocols like MQTT and CoAP are central to my role, with MQTT implementations supporting secure device communication across 500+ endpoints. Python is used for prototyping sensor algorithms and automating test scripts, while REST API design has been critical for linking edge devices to cloud analytics platforms. Go appears in occasional scripting tasks for lightweight service communication, and network automation tools like Ansible have been applied to streamline firmware deployment across 200+ devices. RTOS development remains a core focus, with contributions to FreeRTOS and Zephyr frameworks that improved system responsiveness by 25% in critical monitoring applications.  

Projects  
A key project involved redesigning the firmware architecture for VitalTech’s FDA-cleared glucose monitoring system, which reduced firmware update downtime by 40% through modular code structure. Another initiative focused on integrating secure CoAP protocols into a remote patient monitoring platform, achieving 99.95% packet delivery in field trials. I also spearheaded the development of a custom edge computing module for real-time vital signs analysis, leveraging ARM Cortex-M processors to process data locally and reduce cloud dependency. A recent project involved creating a Python-based toolchain for automated testing of embedded hardware, cutting validation cycles by 30% through simulated stress scenarios.  

Certifications  
Certified Embedded Systems Engineer (CES-E), IEEE (2020). Advanced Topics in Medical Device Software, FDA (2019).  

Languages  
English (professional), Mandarin (fluent).  

Awards & Achievements  
Recognized as a top mentor at VitalTech for fostering a 30% improvement in team productivity through structured RTOS training. Featured in a 2022 industry report on scalable embedded solutions for healthcare, highlighting contributions to edge computing frameworks. Received a commendation for leading the development of a HIPAA-compliant firmware update protocol that minimized security risks during device deployment.
